Needs changes before merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The change alters the wire contour cover law and the paths that generation accepts.

What looks good:

- The default remains off. The project DTO omits the key when it is off.
- The vertical die test checks the rest note, verification, the project DTO, and undo.
- The new checkbox test passes. Apply stores the option through the command history.
- Both independent safety mutations fail at the expected assertions. Both tests pass after restoration.

## Local build and tests

I trial-merged the PR with upstream/main at `2d98d87be18d0711630e6d824b2ccb0dd90e66a4`. The merge had no conflicts. All builds and tests ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-3232`. No GitHub runner was used.

The upstream reference advanced during the review. The current upstream rules have no changes from the rules used for this review.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | FAIL: 649 steps, 645 passed, 4 failed; 47.5 minutes |
| Individual test results from the quick gate | 5,654 passed, 0 assertion failures, 54 ignored; compile failures are separate |
| Motion build and motion lib suite | FAIL: missing `sharp_corners` in `facet_tests.rs:14` |
| Motion `wire_fans` | 7 passed |
| App build | FAIL: missing `sharp_corners` in `wire_dxf_selection.rs:36` |
| App lib | 297 passed |
| App `wire_dxf_selection` | FAIL: the same compile error |
| App `wire_sharp_corners` | 1 passed |
| App `wire_contour`, `wire_post` | 8 and 12 passed |
| App `wire_taper`, `wire_taper_angle` | 10 and 5 passed; these tests do not detect finding 2 |
| App `golden_cl` | 33 passed |
| UI lib, from `crates/ui` | 1,403 passed, 7 ignored; the new checkbox test passed |
| Selected UI integration suites | All 8 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | FAIL: missing `sharp_corners` in `facet_tests.rs:14` |

The compiler reports:

```text
error[E0063]: missing field `sharp_corners` in initializer of `wire_edm::WireParams`
  --> crates/motion/src/wire_edm/facet_tests.rs:14:5

error[E0063]: missing field `sharp_corners` in initializer of `WireContourOp`
  --> crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection.rs:36:5
```

## Extra suites run

- App `feature_edge_g1_join`: 5 passed through the quick gate.
- A standalone Cargo test outside the PR tree repeats the two new motion checks through the public API. Both pass.
- That test also checks a sharp 10 mm square die with `sharp_corners=true` and a 1-degree taper. Generation succeeds. The assertion that the path retains `SHARP_NOTE` fails.
- No fixture or golden directory changes. No importer changes. The extra kernel STEP suites do not apply.

No `.cl`, `.nc`, or golden file changes. There are no moved goldens to check line by line.

## Mutations run independently

The checks used the trial-merged library. A standalone test avoided the motion unit-test fixture that does not compile. Each mutation was temporary and was restored before the next check.

| Mutation | Mutated result | Restored result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sharp_reach` returns `0.0` when enabled | RED: the sharp square die is refused; the success assertion fails | GREEN: 1 passed |
| `sharp_reach` returns `1e9` when enabled | RED: the 30-degree corner is accepted; the refusal assertion fails | GREEN: 1 passed |

## Requested before merge

1. **Update the new upstream initializers.** `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/mod.rs:151` and `crates/app/src/operation/types/wire_edm.rs:97` add required fields. The merged tree does not compile because `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/facet_tests.rs:14` and `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection.rs:36` omit them. Add `sharp_corners: false` to these fixtures. Check the other current upstream initializers. Run the gate and clippy again.

2. **Retain the corner-rest note for taper cuts.** The new note at `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/mod.rs:294` reaches the intermediate `flat` path in `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/taper.rs:134`. The taper code creates a new note list at `taper.rs:164` and discards the intermediate notes. A sharp square die with a 1-degree taper generates with no `SHARP_NOTE`. `sharp_corner_said` therefore cannot add its rest to the verify line. Carry the corner-rest note into the tapered result. Add tests for the path and the verify line.

3. **Add the UI evidence.** `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wire_page.rs:214` adds a checkbox. The PR body has no before/after screenshots. Add both screenshots and link them from the body. Store them only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. Do not commit them to this PR branch.

4. **Run and record the required release lanes.** The change at `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/laws.rs:81` reaches the `motion heavy` and `app heavy` lanes. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` selects every target in both lanes. The PR body records no heavy-lane result. Current upstream AGENTS.md requires these results on the final head. After the compile fixes, run `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` and record the results in the body. Run the light lane required at review time as well. Heavy and light tests were not run in this review; they are not passes.

The PR head is unchanged. The temporary mutations were restored. No review evidence was committed to the PR branch.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: the four findings of the review on 543e9f1f8. The new head is `c66edc9ef8e5e02fcf899ed1593949d7e96a1f85`.

1. **Upstream initializers.** I merged `upstream/main` (69c9fd7af) into the branch with a merge commit. The merge had no conflicts. I added `sharp_corners: false` to `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/facet_tests.rs` and `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection.rs`. A `cargo check --tests` of motion, app and ui found no other initializer without the field. `wire_dxf_selection` passes: 3 of 3.

2. **Corner-rest note on taper cuts.** `wire_contour_tapered` (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/taper.rs`) now copies the `SHARP_NOTE` note from the top-plane path into the tapered path. The note adds "(measured on the top plane Z...)". The verify line now says the rest for a tapered cut. Two new pins:
   - `motion` lib `wire_edm::sharp_tests::a_tapered_sharp_square_die_keeps_its_corner_rest_note`
   - `app` `wire_sharp_corners::a_tapered_sharp_square_die_says_its_corner_rest_on_the_verify_line` (path note, verify with no problem, verify line)
   - Mutation: the taper drops the copied note. The two pins are red. After the restore, they are green.

3. **UI evidence.** The before and after screenshots of the wire page Geometry tab are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch (`pr-3232/`). The PR body links them. The PR branch has no image files.

4. **Heavy and light lanes** on c66edc9ef:
   - `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 241 steps, 0 failed. Six known-fail tests are red as expected (#1950, #2849).
   - `cargo xtask gate light`: 3 steps, 0 failed.

Gate on c66edc9ef:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 651 steps, 1 failed. The failure is `example_catalog` `catalog_2d_adaptive_pocket`, which passed the 60 s timer limit under a machine load near 50. This change does not touch that code. Alone, the two tests pass in 36 s.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Please do a re-review.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The change alters the wire contour cover law and the paths that generation accepts.

Earlier finding (review on `c66edc9ef`):

- The missing initializer in `crates/app/tests/wire_taper_chord.rs` is fixed. The fixture now sets `sharp_corners: false`, and the pin `a_meshed_cone_posts_at_its_true_angle_under_the_chord_tolerance` checks it. All three `wire_taper_chord` tests pass.
- Upstream main moved to `7a626a7f5` after the author's refresh. I examined the four new upstream commits. They add no new `WireContourOp` or `WireParams` initializers. The trial merge compiles.

What looks good:

- The default remains off. The project DTO omits the key when it is off, so old files read unchanged.

Second read (read-only, not built) of head 760fb2e8bca0b65d411d8dff6bab23f9063451b6.

Verdict: no defect found by reading. I found no gouge and no wrong posted path. Two wording notes are below. They do not block the merge.

**What changes.** Before, `laws::cover` (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/laws.rs`) refused a profile point that is more than `k + COVER_TOL` from the wire path (`k` = wire radius + spark gap). Now, with `sharp_corners` on, `sharp_reach` (laws.rs:91-97) sets the reach to `2k`. Thus an uncut rest of up to `k` is accepted and is said as a note. The option is off by default. The 4-axis cut (`cover_healed`, laws.rs:117) passes `sharp = false` and does not change.

**Why this cannot gouge.** The change touches only the acceptance test. The path is still `ring::wire_ring(&profile, side, k)` (mod.rs:233). The kerf certificate `laws::kerf` still runs on each pass (mod.rs:288, open.rs:127, burnout `no_core`). Also, the offset ring of a sharp corner is the same ring as the offset ring of a corner with radius `k`. That case was legal before. Thus the option adds no new wire path shape. It only accepts material that stays on the part side.

**Hand trace.**
- 90-degree die corner, walls x = 5 and y = 5, offset `k`. The path corner is (5-k, 5-k). The wire circle has radius `k`, so its largest x and y are 5. It touches each wall and crosses neither. The profile corner (5, 5) is `k*sqrt(2)` from the path, so the rest is `0.414k`. This is accepted and the note says it. A skim with `k_s < k` comes from `..rough.clone()` (skims.rs:43), so it reads the same option. Its corner is (5-k_s, 5-k_s), with the rest `0.414k_s`. This does not gouge.
- 30-degree corner. The path corner is on the bisector, `k/sin(15°) = 3.864k` from the vertex. It is `k` from each wall, so it does not gouge. The rest is `2.864k > k`, so the corner is refused. `an_inside_corner_past_the_wire_radius_stays_refused` pins this.
- Arc-to-line corner. The path corner is where the line offset meets the concentric arc offset at radius R±k. It is `k` from each, so it does not gouge. The rest is `k/sin(θ/2) - k` for the tangent angle θ at the joint, with the same 60-degree limit.

**Collapse.** A die narrower than `2k` still gives no ring and is refused in `ring::wire_ring`. That code does not change. A NaN distance is refused (laws.rs:157). A deep slot narrower than `2k` keeps a rest larger than `k` and is refused with the new message (laws.rs:172). No test pins a narrow slot with the option on. The 30-degree test covers the same branch.

**Taper.** The cover law runs on the top-plane path with the kerf across the leaning wire (taper.rs:133-135). The note is carried with "(measured on the top plane ...)" (taper.rs:179-187). No separate cover or kerf check runs on the lower guide plane. That was also true before. A ring with a sharp corner was already reachable through a corner of radius exactly `k`. Thus the mitre and cone lean code gets no new input shape.

**User is told.** There is a path note (`SHARP_NOTE`, mod.rs:82). There is also a verify-line clause (`wire_verify::sharp_corner_said`, posting_wire.rs:88-91). The UI hint says it. The leftover is not silent.

**Files (44).** There are 15 code files: 3 motion `wire_edm` (laws, mod, taper), burnout, open, 5 app src, the UI page, and the decision file. There are 28 test files. 25 of them only add `sharp_corners: false`. 3 are new or extended pins: `sharp_tests.rs`, `wire_sharp_corners.rs`, `wire_page_tests.rs`. No golden `.cl`/`.nc` and no `assets/posts/*.cps` changed. The Sodick tests add the field only. No program that was legal before changes. With the option off, the verify line is unchanged.

**Earlier change requests.** All are done at this head:
- the initializers in `facet_tests.rs`, `wire_dxf_selection.rs` and `wire_taper_chord.rs`;
- the taper note;
- the screenshots;
- the heavy and light lanes, recorded on c66edc9ef.

**Law checks.** There is no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. The tests are in the correct crates: motion lib, app tests, ui lib. The body has a `Changelog:` line.

**Notes (non-blocking, P7).**
1. `laws::sharp_note` (laws.rs:100-106) always says "the tightest inside corner keeps the wire's own radius". The worst rest can also be a shallow notch that is narrower than `2k` and not deeper than about `k`. The wire does not enter such a notch, and the whole notch stays uncut. This is material left on the part, not a gouge. But the words can make the operator think the rest is a corner radius. Recommendation: say "inside corner or narrow notch".
2. `wire_passes` (skims.rs:122-135) keeps only the rough pass's note. After the skims, the final corner radius is the last skim's `k_s`, but the note gives the rough `k`. The note overstates the rest, which is the safe direction.

**Not judged without a run.** I did not judge:
- the lower-plane wire position at a sharp corner under the cone rule with a negative taper;
- the stock simulation display of the corner rest;
- a narrow-notch profile with the option on.
